newsitem.title: UK: Refinery margins soar as world crude prices slump.
newsitem.headline: Refinery margins soar as world crude prices slump.

text.p: Oil refinery margins soared in all regions last week, with Asia leading the charge, as crude prices tumbled to new nine-month lows.
Refinery output dropped in value but not as markedly as crude, allowing operators to enjoy profits not seen since last May, according to Reuters price data using standard product yields.

A complex refinery in Singapore returned a high of $6.35 a barrel last week running Dubai crude, before slipping back slightly on Friday to a margin of $6.17, some $3 more than the Mediterranean, the world's next most profitable region.
Profits in Singapore averaged $5.19 a barrel in March.

Solid product markets in Asia mean gas oil is worth a third more than in Europe, naphtha earns $30 a tonne more and gasoline once again has more than a $10 premium over Dubai crude, up from below $9 last week.

Margins in Europe and the Mediterranean also saw a healthy recovery last week on the back of crude's slump, consolidating their recovery from the slim profitability suffered in February and early March.
A complex refinery in Rotterdam saw margins improve by 25 percent to over $2.50 a barrel, from an average of $2.04 in the last week in March.
Hydroskimming plants in Europe running regional oils had the world's weakest margins at $1.26 a barrel, below plants in the Med refining Urals crude, which enjoy a margin of $1.73 a barrel.
Complex refiners in the Mediterranean saw profits rocket by nearly a dollar to $3.20 a barrel from the previous week's $2.26.
In the U.S. Gulf, refiners running a barrel of Brent crude priced after Friday's sharp fall in values would make a profit of $2.37, up sharply from the end-March average of $2.11.
A U.S. Gulf refiner running West Texas intermediate (WTI) would see a margin of $1.48, according to price data.
This compares with a 48-cent profit for U.S.-refined Brent and zero cents for U.S.-processed WTI in the first week of March.
